subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler inference - latency/throughput benchmarks & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@acmeai.com>, Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acmeai.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood follow-up — latency/throughput next steps

Alex / Sarah — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Recap from our side: you mentioned the main evaluation goals are (a) 95th/99th latency under production traffic shape, (b) sustained tokens/sec throughput for batch inference, and (c) delta in latency when using prefix caching / KV cache. You also flagged that cost-per-token and burst behavior are gating factors for your infra team.

2) What Redwood can do now: we shared our high-level differentiators vs hyperscalers — unified serving runtime that supports continuous batching, KV-cache, quantization profiles, and smart routing/fallbacks. For the benchmark we recommend measuring: p50/p95/p99 latency (for both < 128 and > 1024 seq lengths), tokens/sec (sustained over 5/10 minute windows), and end-to-end tail behavior with realistic inter-request timing.

3) Proposed A/B test matrix (quick):
   - Variant A: Acme baseline on hyperscaler model endpoint (your existing setup)
   - Variant B: Redwood default config (single-tenant model, default batcher)
   - Variant C: Redwood with KV-cache enabled and tuned batch windows
   - Variant D: Redwood quantized model (if you want cost/throughput tradeoff)

4) Action items / asks from Acme: sample workload (1k–5k request traces or a 30-minute traffic replay), representative prompt sizes, and the model name/weights you want to compare. Also let us know any enforced regional constraints.

I attached a short lab guide and our initial latency comparison doc to make it easier for your infra team to run the first pass. Dev (cc) will share the test scripts and exact measurement commands.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync next Tuesday (Feb 24) 11:00am PT to review the test plan and assign owners? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up — benchmark scripts & measurement details

Alex / Sarah — quick technical follow-up with details you can hand to your infra team. I also attached the benchmark scripts that automate the traffic replay and metric collection. Highlights: 

- Measurement definitions: p95/p99 measured on end-to-end token-stream completion (from request send to final token flush). tokens/sec = total generated tokens / steady-state window (we recommend 5 min). Report both per-second and per-request tokens/sec.
- Important test knobs: batch size, max-latency threshold (cutoff for batch flush), KV-cache hit/miss scenarios, model precision (fp16 vs int8 quantized), and warm vs cold-start runs.
- Suggested harness: run each variant for at least 10 minutes steady-state, discard the first 2 minutes as warm-up, and capture p50/p95/p99, mean tokens/sec, 95% confidence interval.

Attached: benchmark-scripts.tar.gz (includes runner.sh, measurement.py, and an example config). If you can share a small sample trace (1k requests) I can pre-run locally and push an initial p95 summary so we have numbers to compare on Tuesday.

If you want we can also instrument a lightweight Prometheus + Grafana endpoint so you can pull the histograms directly.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acmeai.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up — initial A/B results & questions

Marissa / Dev — thanks for the materials. We ran a quick A/B pass this morning (our internal baseline vs Redwood default) using a 30-minute replay of production-like traces. High level results attached (acme-test-logs.zip) and inline summary: 

- Hyperscaler baseline: p95 = 210 ms, p99 = 420 ms, sustained tokens/sec = 8.6
- Redwood default (single-tenant): p95 = 170 ms, p99 = 360 ms, sustained tokens/sec = 11.2

Observations / Questions: 
1) These numbers look promising for Redwood. Two quick clarifications: how are you measuring tokens/sec (tokenization differences between model runtimes can skew results)?
2) What batch sizes were used in the Redwood run? We saw occasional spikes during synthetic bursts that pushed p99 above 400ms in one window.
3) Can Redwood reproduce the experiment with KV-cache enabled so we can see delta on the 50–200 token prompt sizes? That’s the most common pattern for our customers.

We attached detailed logs. Happy to jump on a quick call with Dev to walk through them. Also looping Sarah from infra for anything infra-specific.

—
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Systems, Acme AI
alex@acmeai.com

Attachments: acme-test-logs.zip
